core_obligations: Reduce to the universal case (proof lines 405-436): writing the image of the generator x as a polynomial in the generator y with coefficients lambda_i, the condition that this defines a ring map is the displayed relation among the coefficients; introducing the universal polynomial ring in b and the lambda_i together with the element a defined by that relation gives a universal map and a commutative square over the original one which is compatible with the trace maps, so it suffices to prove the statement for the universal map.

Case of degrees below p minus one (proof lines 438-458): expand the product of the (i+1)-st power of the image polynomial with its derivative and observe that the expression is the derivative of the (i+1)-st power; hence all coefficients of powers congruent to minus one modulo p vanish, which is precisely the vanishing of the coefficient of the top power that has to be checked.

Case of degree p minus one (proof lines 460-492): here one works over the integers modulo p, rewrites the expression as the derivative of the p-th power divided by p, and uses the vanishing of the intermediate binomial coefficients modulo p to reduce the p-th power to the sum of the p-th powers of the monomials; after applying the derivative and reducing modulo the defining relation one obtains for the top coefficient exactly the expression appearing in the differential of the defining relation, which proves the compatibility.
proof_roadmap: Use the universal ring in the coefficients to reduce to a single case, checking that the reduction is compatible with the trace maps.
Verify the coefficients of the top power vanish for degrees below p minus one by recognizing a derivative.
Treat the remaining degree over the integers modulo p, where the binomial coefficients in the middle vanish and the p-th power becomes a sum of p-th powers of monomials.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a homomorphism between the two Artin-Schreier like quotients of polynomial rings the trace computed using the source generator equals the trace computed using the target generator composed with the homomorphism (statement lines 399-403). The proof (proof lines 405-498) reduces to the universal case by introducing the universal coefficient ring, and then verifies the required coefficient identities in two cases, using that the expressions are derivatives and, in the remaining case, the vanishing of the intermediate binomial coefficients modulo p. H3: a long explicit computation with a universal reduction, written out in full.
